sources.citation: Kantor Bahasa Maluku. 2020. Antologi Cerita Rakyat Kepulauan Kei.
sources.note: Kei-archipelago folktale anthology from the same office (Kur island is administratively in Kepulauan Kei); may name Kur informants or carry a Kur text, but almost certainly no phonology. Listed only so it is not re-chased.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1. Languoid kurr1245 'Kur'; reference records 43011 (Collins 1982) and 152212 (Loski & Loski 1989).
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Zero grammar/phonology/sketch references; the five listed items are two von Rosenberg overviews, Collins 1982 (subclassification comment cites pp. 122-123), Loski & Loski 1989 (overview/comparative, covers c. 43 East Seram varieties incl. Teor and Kur), and the Ribbe 1903 wordlist.

sources.citation: Loski, Russell A. & Gail M. Loski. 1989. The languages indigenous to Eastern Seram and adjacent islands. In W. D. Laidig (ed.), Maluku (Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 6), 103-142. Ambon: UNPATTI-SIL.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: SIL survey that explicitly covers Kur among c. 43 East Seram varieties (Glottolog record); WILC survey chapters often carry phonological notes and wordlists with stress marked. sil.org blocked (not reachable by automated download) by automated download.
sources.venue: Maluku (Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 6)

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press. Section 11.4 'Teor-Kur', pp. 464-468 (open access, Zenodo 18323007).
sources.note: Nothing. Section 11.4 is historical phonology (sound correspondences) only. p. 464: 'Data is extremely scarce for both languages.. The only data for Kur we have been able to access is the word list in von Rosenberg (1867: 108-114), as well as two folktales, Ohoiwutun (2021) and Rado (2021), published by the Indonesian language office.' Kur forms are cited from the booklets in Indonesian orthography with no prosodic marking; no stress or accent remark anywhere in the section.

sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing: location and dialectometry (85-100% difference from Kei and Yamdena) only; no fonologi/bunyi/tekanan/aksen/nada content.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en). 'Teor-Kur language' (redirect target of 'Kur language'), accessed 2026-09-17.
sources.note: Nothing; classification and speaker numbers only, references limited to Ethnologue and Grimes & Edwards 2026.

sources.citation: Arivina da Costa, Romilda & Muhamad Akib Tatroman. 2021. Metafora dalam konsep warna pada masyarakat penutur bahasa Kur di Pulau Kur, Provinsi Maluku. Prosiding Konferensi Linguistik Tahunan Atma Jaya (KOLITA) 19, 13-15 Juli 2021, 363-367. Jakarta: Pusat Kajian Bahasa dan Budaya, Universitas Katolik Indonesia Atma Jaya. (CORE record dated 2024; oai:ojs.pkp.sfu.ca:article/5818.)
sources.note: No phonology content. The paper is a lexical-semantic study: an 18-item list of Kur colour terms (alfuil, arbir, billau, ankunil, arnara, alselap, atmitan, arkur, atbuit, fukrek, muk tafin, kanfuan, etc., p. 365) in plain orthography without stress or length marking, followed by tenor/vehicle metaphor analysis and a short sociogeographic note on Kur island (p. 365). No section on bunyi/fonologi, no remark on tekanan, aksen or nada anywhere in the text (searched and read in full, pp. 363-367).
sources.venue: Prosiding Konferensi Linguistik Tahunan Atma Jaya (KOLITA) 19

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2019. Kur [kuv]. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 22nd edition. Dallas: SIL International (Internet Archive copy 2019-06-06).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No typology or phonology field: population, location (west Kei Kecil district, Kur and surrounding islands), status 6b*, dialect/intelligibility note and lexical-similarity percentages (47-50% Kei, 71-83% Teor, 41% Watubela, 38% Geser), 'Vigorous. Also use Kei', Muslim. Nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa. n.d. [2017-]. 'Bahasa Kur, Provinsi Maluku'. Bahasa dan Peta Bahasa di Indonesia (petabahasa), entry idb=380.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Location and dialectometry only ('isolek Kur merupakan sebuah bahasa karena persentase perbedaannya dengan bahasa lain di Maluku berkisar 85%-100%, misalnya bahasa Kei dan Yamdena'); no phonology, nothing on stress or tone. Indicates Badan Bahasa holds an unpublished Kur field vocabulary but no published description.

sources.citation: Taber, Mark (ed.), with Pat Andrews, Gail Loski, Jhonny Tjia et al. 1996. Atlas bahasa tanah Maluku. Ambon: Pusat Pengkajian dan Pengembangan Maluku, Universitas Pattimura / Summer Institute of Linguistics. Entry 'Teor-Kur', p. 90 (SIL Language & Culture Archives 37652).
sources.note: No phonology content: location, two dialects (Teor, Kur), Teor settlers on Ut and in Gaur Kristen, c. 5,000 speakers, 'Belum banyak penelitian dilakukan terhadap bahasa tersebut, dan para ahli bahasa berbeda pendapat dalam mengelompokkannya', access routes, classification Austronesian > CMP > Teor-Kur. Unlike neighbouring entries (e.g. Yamdena p. 91) it prints no 'Contoh Bahasa' sample words. scanned extract.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 1991. Sound change and migration distance. In Robert Blust (ed.), Currents in Pacific linguistics: papers on Austronesian languages and ethnolinguistics in honour of George W. Grace (Pacific Linguistics C-117), 27-42. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.note: Nothing. The only mention (pp. 33-34, section MOLUCCAS): 'Only two Moluccan languages, Teor-Kur and Buru, are known to reflect initial and intervocalic *p invariably as [p].' a full-text search for stress/accent the 16-page text for stress/accent/tone/tonal/penult: one hit, a Benedict 1984 title in the references ('a tonal Chamic language on Hainan').

sources.citation: Hughes, Jock. 1987. The languages of Kei, Tanimbar and Aru: a lexicostatistic classification. NUSA 27: 71-111. Section 2.1.2.2 'Teor-Kur', p. 84.
sources.note: Nothing (as recorded in the sibling teor1240 check, which scanned and read the section): only segmental dialect notes, Kur word-final alveolars correspond to Ut palatals, Kur velar nasals to Ut voiced velar plosives. No stress/accent in the paper.

sources.citation: Collins, James T. 1982. Linguistic Research in Maluku: A Report of Recent Field Work. Oceanic Linguistics 21(1/2): 73-146, esp. pp. 122-123 (Teor-Kur).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Only professional linguist's first-hand field report on Teor-Kur; Collins's Maluku field notes sometimes include a line on stress and a short phonological sketch, so pp. 122-123 are the single most likely place for a stress remark.

sources.citation: Ribbe, Carl. 1903. 68 Woerter in 34 verschiedenen Sprachen und Dialekten der Sued-See, der papuanischen und der malayischen Inseln. In Zwei Jahre unter den Kannibalen der Salomo-Inseln, 196-212. Dresden: Elbgau (archive.org zweijahreunterd01kalbgoog).
sources.note: Nothing. The table has a 'Koor' column (68 unaccented forms, e.g. nongbie, menrana, memvina, bobobor, tata, inan); no accent marks and no note on stress. The only pronunciation note (p. 184) concerns the vowels of the Shortlands (Alu) language.
sources.venue: Zwei Jahre unter den Kannibalen der Salomo-Inseln

sources.citation: Riedel, Johan Gerard Friedrich. 1886. De sluik- en kroesharige rassen tusschen Selebes en Papua. 's-Gravenhage: Martinus Nijhoff. xi+486 pp., platen.
sources.note: nothing

sources.citation: von Rosenberg, C. B. H. 1878. Der Malayische Archipel: Land und Leute in Schilderungen. Leipzig: Gustav Weigel. 'b. Die Inseln Koor und Tijoor' pp. 352-355; 'II. Vergleichendes Woerterverzeichniss' pp. 597 ff., column 13 Koor (archive.org dermalayischearc00rose).
sources.note: Nothing. a full-text search for stress/accent/Betonung/Aussprache/Tonzeichen gives no hits in the whole book; the Koor section (pp. 352-355) is ethnographic (population c. 100 in Kilmas, Muslim, Bandanese origin tradition); the wordlist table scanned is garbled, and per Grimes & Edwards 2026 fn. 13 it is only a re-orthographised copy of the 1867 list.

sources.citation: von Rosenberg, C. B. H. 1867. Reis naar de zuidoostereilanden, gedaan in 1865. 's Gravenhage: Martinus Nijhoff. Vergelijkende woordenlijst, Koor column, pp. 108-114; notes pp. 105-107 (archive.org reis-naar-de-zuidoostereilanden).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 107 transcription note only: 'is gebruik gemaakt van de accenten der fransche taal boven de e.. en van de teekens [breve] om aan te toonen dat eene lettergreep kort en [macron] dat zij lang is' (accents mark vowel quality of e and syllable quantity, not stress). p. 106 note on Koor: the small resident population descends from emigrated Bandanese, so its dialect resembles Eli-Ellat (Banda); no accent marks for stress in the Koor column.

sources.citation: Marshall, Craig. ca. 2025. 479-item Teor word list (unpublished; supplied to Grimes & Edwards 2026, fn. 12 p. 464).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only modern phonetic transcription of the sister variety Teor; if it marks stress or has audio it would be the first usable primary evidence for stress placement in Teor-Kur (Kur would still need its own check).

sources.citation: Ohoiwutun, Ida. 2021. Batu penyu / Faut pen / The stone turtle. Ambon: Kantor Bahasa Provinsi Maluku.

sources.note: One of only two modern Kur-language publications; Kantor Bahasa bilingual booklets sometimes carry a short orthography/pronunciation preface. Low chance of a stress statement but the only recent primary Kur material.
